title: Ravel at a Victor rehearsal and Bix's part in Grofe's suite
summary: Ravel visited a rehearsal and noticed Hazlett's subtone; Bix rehearsed his part in a Grofe suite, though not a strong reader.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Yes, I think they became members of the band by then. The band went out and didn't do anything at one particular time, but as far as the recordings now, I want to get back to -- we went along with Victor for quite awhile and we made a bunch of records over at Leiderkrautz and then they -- let's see, at one of the rehearsals over there, Ravel came and visited and we were in the control room and he wanted to know what's that sound. It was Chester's subtone. He hadn't heard anything like that before. They wanted him to evaluate Ferde's compositions. Ferde was making the Grand Canyon Suite and it was another one, another suite that he did before that. The one that Bix played in, the only one he played in as a matter of fact. He wrote a part out for Bix and I remember Bix coming to the rehearsal and going over and over it, rehearsing it and rehearsing it, and he had the reputation of not being able to read so well.

He was no great reader, but he could read, as long as he had guys like Trumbauer and the other guys alongside of him, he knew where he was. Well, let's see, so there was something else I wanted to get said there.
